title: Per-message extraction batch
description: What a worker may return about a batch of messages. Deliberately free of any duration or amount: those are computed by deterministic code from the counts below. See observe/llm/schema_guard.py, which rejects any response carrying one anyway.

msg_uid.description: Echo back exactly the id given for this message.

is_operational.description: True if this is the company's work. False for social, personal, newsletter or administrative-chatter messages.

process_phrase.description: A short canonical phrase naming the specific recurring activity, lowercase, verb first, no dates or names. For example 'confirm nomination change with pipeline scheduler'. This is clustered later; consistent phrasing across messages matters more than elegance.

rework_signal.description: The message shows something being redone, corrected, or having been wrong.

waiting_signal.description: The message shows someone blocked, chasing, or waiting on another party.

manual_transfer_signal.description: The message shows data being moved between systems or documents by hand: re-keying, copy-paste, pasting a table into mail, reading numbers off one screen into another.

deadline_signal.description: The message names a cutoff, deadline or time pressure.

actors_named.description: How many distinct people are named as doing part of this work in the visible text. A cross-check only; participant counts come from the headers.

evidence.description: Quotes that would let a sceptical reader verify the classification. Copy the words EXACTLY as they appear; they are used as a search key against the raw file and a quote that cannot be located is discarded.
